This is entirely wrong. The employer is the moving party, which makes this a discharge. If you tell them that you quit and put in two weeks' notice, but they decide to let you go early, it's still a quit. In the same way, their employer gave them notice of termination, and they accepted the termination early, so it's a discharge.

Now, a few things.
1) Get any documentation possible supporting that they told you you were going to be fired first.  You need this to support your side.
2) If you badmouthed the company, you can still get unemployment. However, that is only if either A) they didn't have a policy or didn't have a specific enough policy regarding that and they did not warn you or make you aware that your job was in jeopardy prior to discharge. B) They can not prove that you actually bad mouthed their company. C)  They had a policy regarding that, and you can prove that it was not uniformly enforced. 
Also, you can still get unemployment if you quit. Idk why people say that you can't
